note: Not approved or active. Original curriculum practice bank for academic reviewer and editorial QA; does not grant a credential.

questions.stem: What is the purpose of graphic design in this course?
options: Communicate defined information clearly through visual organization
Make every element decorative
Ignore the reader's actual needs
Assume software automatically determines hierarchy
questions.rationale: Design is more than surface decoration. Source: MAIC Fundamentals of Graphic Design, page 2.

questions.stem: Why does a designer need a specified audience?
options: Treat draft sketches as final certifications
Use any online brand assets without rights
Readers' context influences layout and information priority
Make every element decorative
questions.rationale: Audience needs shape design decisions. Source: MAIC Fundamentals of Graphic Design, page 2.

questions.stem: What is a design brief used for?
options: Ignore the reader's actual needs
To document goals, constraints, content and delivery requirements
Assume software automatically determines hierarchy
Treat draft sketches as final certifications
questions.rationale: The brief guides visual choices. Source: MAIC Fundamentals of Graphic Design, page 2.

questions.stem: Why can a visually attractive poster still fail?
options: Use any online brand assets without rights
It may make required information hard to find or read
Make every element decorative
Ignore the reader's actual needs
questions.rationale: Aesthetic appeal does not guarantee comprehension. Source: MAIC Fundamentals of Graphic Design, page 2.

questions.stem: Which outcome better measures a workshop poster's usefulness?
options: Assume software automatically determines hierarchy
Treat draft sketches as final certifications
Use any online brand assets without rights
A viewer can identify the correct date, place and action
questions.rationale: Practical comprehension is tied to the poster's purpose. Source: MAIC Fundamentals of Graphic Design, page 2.

questions.stem: Why should designers retain original approved assets?
options: Make every element decorative
Ignore the reader's actual needs
They are needed for consistent revisions and accurate output
Assume software automatically determines hierarchy
questions.rationale: Source assets support traceability. Source: MAIC Fundamentals of Graphic Design, page 2.

questions.stem: Which design method is software-independent?
options: Treat draft sketches as final certifications
Use any online brand assets without rights
Make every element decorative
Sketching layout hierarchy before using an application
questions.rationale: Design principles apply beyond specific tools. Source: MAIC Fundamentals of Graphic Design, page 2.

questions.stem: What does the course self-assessment represent?
options: Ignore the reader's actual needs
Practice feedback, not official certification
Assume software automatically determines hierarchy
Treat draft sketches as final certifications
questions.rationale: Learning rubrics do not create formal credentials. Source: MAIC Fundamentals of Graphic Design, page 2.

questions.stem: A poster is beautiful but readers cannot find the time or venue. How should it be evaluated?
options: The poster succeeded because the palette is attractive
It is equivalent to a complete registration page
The design failed an essential communication task
A high image resolution proves usability
questions.rationale: The objective is reliable and accessible communication. Source: MAIC Fundamentals of Graphic Design, page 2.

questions.stem: A class uses made-up event details for a design exercise. How should the result be described?
options: As a verified public announcement
As a fictional study example
As a certified official campaign
As actual eyewitness documentation
questions.rationale: Fictional examples must remain visibly hypothetical. Source: MAIC Fundamentals of Graphic Design, page 2.

questions.stem: What information should a design brief identify?
options: Choose a font before finding the event's date
Audience, objective, mandatory text, sizes and rights
Assume all print and digital sizes behave identically
Evaluate success only by design software speed
questions.rationale: A brief addresses both communication and production. Source: MAIC Fundamentals of Graphic Design, page 3.

questions.stem: Why does viewing distance affect poster design?
options: Use a competitor logo as a placeholder without labeling
Ignore source verification of promotional promises
Essential text must remain visible from the intended distance
Choose a font before finding the event's date
questions.rationale: Context determines legibility needs. Source: MAIC Fundamentals of Graphic Design, page 3.

questions.stem: What should be done with an unverified promotional guarantee?
options: Request evidence before presenting it as established
Assume all print and digital sizes behave identically
Evaluate success only by design software speed
Use a competitor logo as a placeholder without labeling
questions.rationale: Marketing claims require substantiation. Source: MAIC Fundamentals of Graphic Design, page 3.

questions.stem: What is an appropriate way to handle a missing approved logo?
options: Ignore source verification of promotional promises
Use a clearly marked placeholder pending the real asset
Choose a font before finding the event's date
Assume all print and digital sizes behave identically
questions.rationale: Do not copy unrelated brand artwork. Source: MAIC Fundamentals of Graphic Design, page 3.

questions.stem: What distinguishes a website graphic from a printed flyer?
options: Their viewing contexts and output requirements differ
Evaluate success only by design software speed
Use a competitor logo as a placeholder without labeling
Ignore source verification of promotional promises
questions.rationale: Different media need different design specifications. Source: MAIC Fundamentals of Graphic Design, page 3.

questions.stem: Why should contact details be checked before layout approval?
options: Choose a font before finding the event's date
Incorrect practical information can undermine the entire design
Assume all print and digital sizes behave identically
Evaluate success only by design software speed
questions.rationale: Factual accuracy is part of graphic design. Source: MAIC Fundamentals of Graphic Design, page 3.

questions.stem: What makes a design success condition useful?
options: Use a competitor logo as a placeholder without labeling
It describes an observable audience task or understanding
Ignore source verification of promotional promises
Choose a font before finding the event's date
questions.rationale: Success can be defined by comprehension. Source: MAIC Fundamentals of Graphic Design, page 3.

questions.stem: What is one benefit of three thumbnail concepts?
options: Assume all print and digital sizes behave identically
They let the designer compare composition alternatives early
Evaluate success only by design software speed
Use a competitor logo as a placeholder without labeling
questions.rationale: Quick sketches support initial decisions. Source: MAIC Fundamentals of Graphic Design, page 3.

questions.stem: A client provides a date but not the registration fee. What should the designer do?
options: Claim all events are free
Publish a guessed amount without a note
Copy a competitor's admission price
Request confirmation instead of inventing that attendance is free
questions.rationale: The brief should not contain unsupported details. Source: MAIC Fundamentals of Graphic Design, page 3.

questions.stem: A poster is to be viewed from several meters away. What should change from a phone-only graphic?
options: Add several paragraphs of tiny explanatory text
Hide the contact details near the edge
Prioritize larger, simpler essential information for the viewing distance
Use only decorative elements
questions.rationale: Reading context drives hierarchy and type scale. Source: MAIC Fundamentals of Graphic Design, page 3.

questions.stem: What is visual hierarchy?
options: Align each block randomly
The ordered emphasis guiding readers through information
Treat font size as unrelated to emphasis
Use a different grid for every repeating card
questions.rationale: Hierarchy establishes reading priorities. Source: MAIC Fundamentals of Graphic Design, page 4.

questions.stem: What does alignment provide in a layout?
options: Fill every margin with decoration
A consistent visual relationship among elements
Scatter related details across the page
Align each block randomly
questions.rationale: Alignment reduces accidental visual noise. Source: MAIC Fundamentals of Graphic Design, page 4.

questions.stem: What is a purpose of a grid?
options: Treat font size as unrelated to emphasis
Repeatable columns, margins and spacing across a design
Use a different grid for every repeating card
Fill every margin with decoration
questions.rationale: Grids support intentional composition. Source: MAIC Fundamentals of Graphic Design, page 4.

questions.stem: Why is white space valuable?
options: Scatter related details across the page
Align each block randomly
Treat font size as unrelated to emphasis
It separates groups and reduces clutter
questions.rationale: Empty area can support comprehension. Source: MAIC Fundamentals of Graphic Design, page 4.

questions.stem: What is an example of related-information grouping?
options: Use a different grid for every repeating card
Placing event date and time close together
Fill every margin with decoration
Scatter related details across the page
questions.rationale: Proximity helps readers interpret relationships. Source: MAIC Fundamentals of Graphic Design, page 4.

questions.stem: Why should the largest text usually communicate a priority?
options: Align each block randomly
Treat font size as unrelated to emphasis
Size is a strong attention cue that can establish meaning
Use a different grid for every repeating card
questions.rationale: Large text should reinforce the primary message. Source: MAIC Fundamentals of Graphic Design, page 4.

questions.stem: What is a risk of random alignment across cards?
options: Information appears inconsistent and harder to scan
Fill every margin with decoration
Scatter related details across the page
Align each block randomly
questions.rationale: Repeated alignment improves order. Source: MAIC Fundamentals of Graphic Design, page 4.

questions.stem: When is an asymmetrical layout acceptable?
options: Treat font size as unrelated to emphasis
Use a different grid for every repeating card
When its balance and reading sequence are intentional
Fill every margin with decoration
questions.rationale: Visual balance need not be perfectly mirrored. Source: MAIC Fundamentals of Graphic Design, page 4.

questions.stem: An announcement needs event title, date and contact details. Which item should normally be prominent?
options: A decorative border with no information
The title or principal event message
An unrelated photograph
A randomly selected minor footnote
questions.rationale: Hierarchy directs first attention to the core message. Source: MAIC Fundamentals of Graphic Design, page 4.

questions.stem: A design uses three columns across a 900-pixel content area with no gaps. How wide is each column?
options: 200 pixels
300 pixels
450 pixels
900 pixels
questions.rationale: 900 divided by three equals 300. Source: MAIC Fundamentals of Graphic Design, page 4.

questions.stem: What distinguishes display typography from body typography?
options: Use a new typeface for every sentence
Stretch typography until it fits
Treat dates as optional decoration
Display type conveys short character while body type prioritizes sustained reading
questions.rationale: Typography roles have different needs. Source: MAIC Fundamentals of Graphic Design, page 5.

questions.stem: Why might thin type on a detailed photograph be ineffective?
options: Foreground and background may lack readable separation
Ignore text direction in translation
Assume low contrast cannot affect reading
Use a new typeface for every sentence
questions.rationale: Readability depends on actual presentation. Source: MAIC Fundamentals of Graphic Design, page 5.

questions.stem: What is a common problem with too many unrelated fonts?
options: Stretch typography until it fits
Treat dates as optional decoration
The hierarchy can become visually inconsistent
Ignore text direction in translation
questions.rationale: Consistent type choices support recognition. Source: MAIC Fundamentals of Graphic Design, page 5.

questions.stem: Why should names and numbers be proofread in design?
options: Assume low contrast cannot affect reading
Use a new typeface for every sentence
Stretch typography until it fits
They convey factual information rather than decoration
questions.rationale: Text accuracy matters in graphics. Source: MAIC Fundamentals of Graphic Design, page 5.

questions.stem: Why test typography at intended device size?
options: Treat dates as optional decoration
Text that looks clear in the editor may be unreadable when scaled
Ignore text direction in translation
Assume low contrast cannot affect reading
questions.rationale: Actual reading scale determines legibility. Source: MAIC Fundamentals of Graphic Design, page 5.

questions.stem: What does line spacing affect?
options: Use a new typeface for every sentence
Stretch typography until it fits
Treat dates as optional decoration
The readability and grouping of multi-line text
questions.rationale: Spacing is part of typographic hierarchy. Source: MAIC Fundamentals of Graphic Design, page 5.

questions.stem: Why should multilingual layouts be individually tested?
options: Ignore text direction in translation
Assume low contrast cannot affect reading
Script direction and text length can change the composition
Use a new typeface for every sentence
questions.rationale: Translation is not a simple fixed-width substitution. Source: MAIC Fundamentals of Graphic Design, page 5.

questions.stem: Which element can remain unchanged across translations?
options: Stretch typography until it fits
Treat dates as optional decoration
An approved nontranslated brand wordmark
Ignore text direction in translation
questions.rationale: Brand identity can be a fixed design asset. Source: MAIC Fundamentals of Graphic Design, page 5.

questions.stem: A flyer body is too small to read at its intended size. What is a correct fix?
options: Make the font even thinner
Stretch letters horizontally
Increase legibility and adjust layout or copy
Reduce contrast further
questions.rationale: Text should be readable in its actual context. Source: MAIC Fundamentals of Graphic Design, page 5.

questions.stem: An English graphic must be localized into Arabic. What should be verified?
options: Only the original English word count
That logos are translated automatically
Script direction, font support and resulting layout
That the old line breaks never change
questions.rationale: Language adaptations can change space and direction. Source: MAIC Fundamentals of Graphic Design, page 5.

questions.stem: Why does a brand palette need functional color roles?
options: Consistent use helps guide attention and identity
Assume all different hues have strong contrast
Apply web standards as universal print law
Ignore the readability of text on images
questions.rationale: Color should support a repeatable design system. Source: MAIC Fundamentals of Graphic Design, page 6.

questions.stem: What does text-background contrast influence?
options: Show warnings through color only
Choose all colors solely by preference
Assume all different hues have strong contrast
How easily text can be read
questions.rationale: Luminance difference affects visibility. Source: MAIC Fundamentals of Graphic Design, page 6.

questions.stem: Under WCAG 2.2 AA, what is the general minimum for normal web text?
options: Apply web standards as universal print law
Ignore the readability of text on images
Show warnings through color only
questions.rationale: The text contrast threshold is generally 4.5 to 1. Source: MAIC Fundamentals of Graphic Design, page 6.

questions.stem: Under WCAG 2.2 AA, what is the general minimum for defined large web text?
options: Choose all colors solely by preference
Assume all different hues have strong contrast
Apply web standards as universal print law
questions.rationale: The large-text contrast threshold is generally 3 to 1. Source: MAIC Fundamentals of Graphic Design, page 6.

questions.stem: Why is contrast checking not the same as choosing different hues?
options: Ignore the readability of text on images
Show warnings through color only
Choose all colors solely by preference
Colors can differ in hue while remaining close in luminance
questions.rationale: Contrast is based on relative luminance. Source: MAIC Fundamentals of Graphic Design, page 6.

questions.stem: Why must a warning not be conveyed by red color alone?
options: Some readers may not perceive the color distinction
Assume all different hues have strong contrast
Apply web standards as universal print law
Ignore the readability of text on images
questions.rationale: Meaning should be supported by labels or symbols. Source: MAIC Fundamentals of Graphic Design, page 6.

questions.stem: Does the cited web contrast threshold govern all print products globally?
options: No, it is a web criterion with stated scope and exceptions
Show warnings through color only
Choose all colors solely by preference
Assume all different hues have strong contrast
questions.rationale: Web accessibility guidance should not be described as universal print law. Source: MAIC Fundamentals of Graphic Design, page 6.

questions.stem: What is a likely problem with low-contrast button labels?
options: Apply web standards as universal print law
Ignore the readability of text on images
Show warnings through color only
Users may not read the action text clearly
questions.rationale: Legibility is required for usable interface design. Source: MAIC Fundamentals of Graphic Design, page 6.

questions.stem: A normal web-text color pair has a contrast ratio of 3.5:1. Does it generally meet WCAG AA minimum?
options: No, the usual threshold is 4.5:1
Yes, the usual threshold is 3:1 for all text
Yes, any ratio above 2:1 is compliant
No, only a 10:1 ratio is allowed
questions.rationale: Normal text generally requires at least 4.5 to one. Source: MAIC Fundamentals of Graphic Design, page 6.

questions.stem: A chart uses red and green to mark errors and successes. What addition helps accessibility?
options: Text labels or meaningful icons alongside the colors
Removing all text labels
Adding more red and green without meaning
Making the colors the only distinction
questions.rationale: Color alone should not convey essential meaning. Source: MAIC Fundamentals of Graphic Design, page 6.

questions.stem: What is a raster image composed of?
options: Assume all JPG files are infinitely scalable
Treat screenshot logos as print masters
Use images that misidentify the actual event
A grid of pixels
questions.rationale: Raster imagery has finite pixel detail. Source: MAIC Fundamentals of Graphic Design, page 7.

questions.stem: What is a major benefit of vector artwork?
options: Use unlicensed photographs without review
Assume every vector file contains no pixels
Paths and shapes can scale without the same raster pixelation
Assume all JPG files are infinitely scalable
questions.rationale: Vectors are suited to scalable logos and illustrations. Source: MAIC Fundamentals of Graphic Design, page 7.

questions.stem: Why is a small logo screenshot poor for large print?
options: Its effective pixel resolution may become visibly inadequate
Treat screenshot logos as print masters
Use images that misidentify the actual event
Use unlicensed photographs without review
questions.rationale: Scaling raster thumbnails can soften detail. Source: MAIC Fundamentals of Graphic Design, page 7.

questions.stem: Why is a vector file extension not proof of entirely vector contents?
options: Assume every vector file contains no pixels
Assume all JPG files are infinitely scalable
Treat screenshot logos as print masters
It may contain embedded raster imagery
questions.rationale: File containers can combine asset types. Source: MAIC Fundamentals of Graphic Design, page 7.

questions.stem: What should be verified before using a stock photograph?
options: Use images that misidentify the actual event
Rights and whether the image truthfully represents the content
Use unlicensed photographs without review
Assume every vector file contains no pixels
questions.rationale: Permitted and accurate imagery matters. Source: MAIC Fundamentals of Graphic Design, page 7.

questions.stem: Why may an unrelated building photograph mislead an event flyer?
options: Assume all JPG files are infinitely scalable
Treat screenshot logos as print masters
Use images that misidentify the actual event
Readers may mistake it for the actual venue
questions.rationale: Illustrative images need appropriate context. Source: MAIC Fundamentals of Graphic Design, page 7.

questions.stem: What determines effective print image resolution?
options: The source pixels in relation to printed size and viewing conditions
Use unlicensed photographs without review
Assume every vector file contains no pixels
Assume all JPG files are infinitely scalable
questions.rationale: Pixels alone do not determine final print clarity. Source: MAIC Fundamentals of Graphic Design, page 7.

questions.stem: What should an editor preserve when modifying a photograph?
options: An appropriate original source for comparison and later correction
Treat screenshot logos as print masters
Use images that misidentify the actual event
Use unlicensed photographs without review
questions.rationale: Source retention supports quality and provenance. Source: MAIC Fundamentals of Graphic Design, page 7.

questions.stem: A 200-pixel-wide logo thumbnail is enlarged to 2,000 pixels. What risk increases?
options: Guaranteed sharper vector detail
Automatic improvement of original photography
A file becomes legally cleared for reuse
Visible raster softness or pixelation
questions.rationale: Large raster enlargement cannot invent source pixel detail. Source: MAIC Fundamentals of Graphic Design, page 7.

questions.stem: A logo must appear on stationery and a very large banner. Which asset type is preferable?
options: A 100-pixel compressed screenshot
A heavily blurred photograph of the logo
An approved editable vector master
A screenshot taken from an unrelated website
questions.rationale: Vector masters are more adaptable across sizes. Source: MAIC Fundamentals of Graphic Design, page 7.

questions.stem: What is part of a visual identity system?
options: Modify a logo's proportions with each new post
Reuse another company's branded course template
Keep no records of design approval
Approved logos, typography, colors and spacing rules
questions.rationale: Identity organizes repeatable visual traits. Source: MAIC Fundamentals of Graphic Design, page 8.

questions.stem: Why can a mobile card differ in layout while retaining the same brand?
options: Translate the approved wordmark arbitrarily
Lock event contact details permanently
Format changes can preserve core recognizable identity elements
Modify a logo's proportions with each new post
questions.rationale: Consistency does not mean identical composition. Source: MAIC Fundamentals of Graphic Design, page 8.

questions.stem: What should remain stable when editing a fixed logo?
options: Reuse another company's branded course template
Approved artwork, proportions and its prescribed styling
Keep no records of design approval
Translate the approved wordmark arbitrarily
questions.rationale: Brand marks should not change arbitrarily. Source: MAIC Fundamentals of Graphic Design, page 8.

questions.stem: What should be included in reusable design components?
options: Lock event contact details permanently
Documented spacing, safe areas and text roles
Modify a logo's proportions with each new post
Reuse another company's branded course template
questions.rationale: Components help prevent inconsistent variants. Source: MAIC Fundamentals of Graphic Design, page 8.

questions.stem: Why should date and contact fields remain editable in templates?
options: Keep no records of design approval
Translate the approved wordmark arbitrarily
Lock event contact details permanently
Each new release has factual information that can change
questions.rationale: Templates need controlled content updates. Source: MAIC Fundamentals of Graphic Design, page 8.

questions.stem: What is a risk of copying an unrelated academy's template?
options: Modify a logo's proportions with each new post
Reuse another company's branded course template
It may reproduce competitor branding or protected design work
Keep no records of design approval
questions.rationale: Original branding and permission are required. Source: MAIC Fundamentals of Graphic Design, page 8.

questions.stem: Why should identity files have revision histories?
options: Translate the approved wordmark arbitrarily
Teams can trace changes and preserve approved versions
Lock event contact details permanently
Modify a logo's proportions with each new post
questions.rationale: Versioning reduces accidental identity drift. Source: MAIC Fundamentals of Graphic Design, page 8.

questions.stem: What is the difference between fixed and localized text?
options: Identity assets may remain unchanged while explanatory copy is translated
Reuse another company's branded course template
Keep no records of design approval
Translate the approved wordmark arbitrarily
questions.rationale: Brand elements and translatable content have different rules. Source: MAIC Fundamentals of Graphic Design, page 8.

questions.stem: A date changes after a flyer template is approved. What should be edited?
options: The approved logo proportions
The permanent brand name
The event date field without altering fixed identity elements
Every color randomly
questions.rationale: Template fields have different levels of editability. Source: MAIC Fundamentals of Graphic Design, page 8.

questions.stem: A logo suddenly becomes tilted on mobile compared with desktop. What is the issue?
options: A violation of fixed identity presentation
A necessary translation choice
A requirement for all phone graphics
Proof of better readability
questions.rationale: Brand assets should remain consistent and upright when specified. Source: MAIC Fundamentals of Graphic Design, page 8.

questions.stem: What is an important goal when designing for a phone screen?
options: Assume every desktop layout fits on a phone unchanged
Use colors as the only chart category indicators
Keep essential information legible at the smaller viewing size
Treat alt text as a substitute for fact checking
questions.rationale: Mobile contexts demand attention to scale. Source: MAIC Fundamentals of Graphic Design, page 9.

questions.stem: Why may desktop columns need to stack vertically?
options: Hide labels behind interface overlays
Reduce essential text until it cannot be read
A narrow screen may not support readable side-by-side content
Assume every desktop layout fits on a phone unchanged
questions.rationale: Responsive layouts can rearrange groups. Source: MAIC Fundamentals of Graphic Design, page 9.

questions.stem: What should remain correct after responsive adaptation?
options: Use colors as the only chart category indicators
Reading order and factual content
Treat alt text as a substitute for fact checking
Hide labels behind interface overlays
questions.rationale: Layout changes must not distort meaning. Source: MAIC Fundamentals of Graphic Design, page 9.

questions.stem: What can happen when text sits behind a fixed app overlay?
options: Reduce essential text until it cannot be read
Assume every desktop layout fits on a phone unchanged
Critical information may become hidden
Use colors as the only chart category indicators
questions.rationale: Safe areas depend on actual interfaces. Source: MAIC Fundamentals of Graphic Design, page 9.

questions.stem: Why use meaningful alternative text for certain digital images?
options: Treat alt text as a substitute for fact checking
Hide labels behind interface overlays
Reduce essential text until it cannot be read
It can communicate important content without visual access
questions.rationale: Accessible descriptions help some users. Source: MAIC Fundamentals of Graphic Design, page 9.

questions.stem: Why avoid using only color to distinguish chart categories?
options: Assume every desktop layout fits on a phone unchanged
Use colors as the only chart category indicators
Treat alt text as a substitute for fact checking
Some people cannot reliably infer meaning from hue alone
questions.rationale: Categories should also use labels or patterns. Source: MAIC Fundamentals of Graphic Design, page 9.

questions.stem: What is the benefit of testing at actual phone scale?
options: Hide labels behind interface overlays
Reduce essential text until it cannot be read
Assume every desktop layout fits on a phone unchanged
It reveals cropping and legibility problems that a large preview misses
questions.rationale: Real target sizes matter. Source: MAIC Fundamentals of Graphic Design, page 9.

questions.stem: When may a link or caption supplement a dense social graphic?
options: Use colors as the only chart category indicators
Treat alt text as a substitute for fact checking
Hide labels behind interface overlays
When detailed information cannot fit legibly inside the image
questions.rationale: An accessible destination can carry necessary detail. Source: MAIC Fundamentals of Graphic Design, page 9.

questions.stem: A desktop banner is 1200 pixels wide and needs a phone variant at 600 pixels wide. What should be prioritized?
options: Recomposition for reading order and legibility, not blind scaling
Reducing every font by exactly half
Cropping the call to action out
Keeping unrelated empty columns
questions.rationale: Responsive adaptation is not mere proportional scaling. Source: MAIC Fundamentals of Graphic Design, page 9.

questions.stem: A mobile graphic's date is covered by a fixed app control. What should the designer change?
options: Assume viewers can guess the date
Move important information into a safe visible area
Remove the date entirely
Make the overlay opaque
questions.rationale: Critical text must remain visible on its target device. Source: MAIC Fundamentals of Graphic Design, page 9.

questions.stem: What is bleed in print preparation?
options: Artwork extending beyond trim to avoid unintended white edges
Put critical information beyond the trim line
Treat a screen preview as final print proof
Use JPEG to preserve alpha transparency
questions.rationale: Print bleed accommodates final trimming. Source: MAIC Fundamentals of Graphic Design, page 10.

questions.stem: Why keep essential text inside safe margins?
options: Trimming can otherwise remove necessary information
Assume every printer uses identical bleed settings
Discard every editable source file
Put critical information beyond the trim line
questions.rationale: Text near the edge is at risk. Source: MAIC Fundamentals of Graphic Design, page 10.

questions.stem: Who should confirm production-specific bleed requirements?
options: The actual printing provider or product specification
Treat a screen preview as final print proof
Use JPEG to preserve alpha transparency
Assume every printer uses identical bleed settings
questions.rationale: Print settings are not one universal value. Source: MAIC Fundamentals of Graphic Design, page 10.

questions.stem: Why export an editable source and a review PDF separately?
options: Discard every editable source file
Put critical information beyond the trim line
Treat a screen preview as final print proof
They serve revision and delivery purposes respectively
questions.rationale: Different file formats serve different stages. Source: MAIC Fundamentals of Graphic Design, page 10.

questions.stem: When is PNG useful compared with JPEG?
options: Use JPEG to preserve alpha transparency
When the output requires supported transparency
Assume every printer uses identical bleed settings
Discard every editable source file
questions.rationale: PNG can preserve transparent areas. Source: MAIC Fundamentals of Graphic Design, page 10.

questions.stem: Why might JPEG be appropriate for a photograph?
options: It can provide efficient photographic image delivery
Put critical information beyond the trim line
Treat a screen preview as final print proof
Use JPEG to preserve alpha transparency
questions.rationale: Format choice depends on image content. Source: MAIC Fundamentals of Graphic Design, page 10.

questions.stem: What should be checked in a print PDF?
options: Assume every printer uses identical bleed settings
Discard every editable source file
Text, embedded fonts, image quality and page specifications
Put critical information beyond the trim line
questions.rationale: Preflight covers technical and factual aspects. Source: MAIC Fundamentals of Graphic Design, page 10.

questions.stem: Why should a correction produce a traceable file version?
options: Treat a screen preview as final print proof
Use JPEG to preserve alpha transparency
Old exports may remain in use and need clear replacement
Assume every printer uses identical bleed settings
questions.rationale: Versioning helps manage published errors. Source: MAIC Fundamentals of Graphic Design, page 10.

questions.stem: A background image should run to the printed page edge. What should the designer verify?
options: That the JPEG name contains print
That all printers require zero bleed
Required bleed and trim conditions with the printer
That text can sit outside the trim line
questions.rationale: Full-bleed print needs suitable production specifications. Source: MAIC Fundamentals of Graphic Design, page 10.

questions.stem: An icon must have a transparent background for digital use. Which format is commonly suitable?
options: A JPEG expecting an alpha channel
PNG with a transparent channel
A flattened opaque photo only
A printed paper scan only
questions.rationale: PNG commonly supports transparency. Source: MAIC Fundamentals of Graphic Design, page 10.

questions.stem: What are the two deliverables in the workshop case?
options: An A4 print poster and a 1080 by 1350-pixel social graphic
Stretch the print artwork regardless of aspect ratio
Use a competitor's logo for convenience
Rotate the brand mark to fill empty space
questions.rationale: The practice brief requests print and social outputs. Source: MAIC Fundamentals of Graphic Design, page 11.

questions.stem: Why not simply stretch the A4 artwork into a vertical social image?
options: Scaling without recomposition may distort hierarchy and logo
Publish a fictional QR placeholder as a live registration link
Ignore the venue address during proofing
Stretch the print artwork regardless of aspect ratio
questions.rationale: Different formats require deliberate adaptation. Source: MAIC Fundamentals of Graphic Design, page 11.

questions.stem: What should be checked about the displayed venue address?
options: It must match the fictional source brief
Use a competitor's logo for convenience
Rotate the brand mark to fill empty space
Publish a fictional QR placeholder as a live registration link
questions.rationale: Practical facts should remain correct. Source: MAIC Fundamentals of Graphic Design, page 11.

questions.stem: Which asset is not permitted in the fictional case?
options: Ignore the venue address during proofing
An unrelated competitor's logo or copied template
Stretch the print artwork regardless of aspect ratio
Use a competitor's logo for convenience
questions.rationale: The brief requires original or approved materials. Source: MAIC Fundamentals of Graphic Design, page 11.

questions.stem: What is the appropriate status of a classroom QR code without a real registration site?
options: Rotate the brand mark to fill empty space
Publish a fictional QR placeholder as a live registration link
Ignore the venue address during proofing
A clearly labeled placeholder
questions.rationale: A fictional link should not be presented as active. Source: MAIC Fundamentals of Graphic Design, page 11.

questions.stem: Why should phone-scale review happen before publishing the social graphic?
options: It catches illegible contact details and unsafe cropping
Stretch the print artwork regardless of aspect ratio
Use a competitor's logo for convenience
Rotate the brand mark to fill empty space
questions.rationale: Device-specific checking improves readability. Source: MAIC Fundamentals of Graphic Design, page 11.

questions.stem: How should an event title translated into a longer language be handled?
options: Publish a fictional QR placeholder as a live registration link
Ignore the venue address during proofing
Reflow text and retest the composition
Stretch the print artwork regardless of aspect ratio
questions.rationale: Language expansion changes layout requirements. Source: MAIC Fundamentals of Graphic Design, page 11.

questions.stem: What should happen if the published poster lists the wrong venue?
options: Use a competitor's logo for convenience
Rotate the brand mark to fill empty space
Publish a fictional QR placeholder as a live registration link
Prepare and distribute a corrected version with clear revision information
questions.rationale: A wrong address is a material error. Source: MAIC Fundamentals of Graphic Design, page 11.

questions.stem: A 1080 by 1350-pixel graphic has what width-to-height ratio?
questions.rationale: Divide width and height by 270 to obtain four to five. Source: MAIC Fundamentals of Graphic Design, page 11.

questions.stem: The workshop runs from 10 a.m. to noon. What duration should the poster convey?
options: 2 hours
1 hour
3 hours
4 hours
questions.rationale: From ten in the morning until noon is two hours. Source: MAIC Fundamentals of Graphic Design, page 11.
